quotes.text: We are deeply concerned that they may be downloading American private and confidential data onto external databases where they are applying artificial intelligence systems to study and understand them,

This resolution will demand answers. This resolution, which has been introduced in the Oversight Committee, will demand that they produce documentation, names, datasets, and information about what they are doing.

H. Res. 286. A resolution of inquiry requesting the President to transmit certain documents relating to the dangerous, unaccountable use of AI by the United States DOGE Service to jeopardize the private information and essential services of the American people; to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

The American people demand to know why Elon Musk and DOGE are hacking our private and sensitive data and what they are doing with it. [...] Today I dropped an oversight resolution demanding the Administration provide answers about what it is doing with our data and how it is using Artificial Intelligence to data mine our systems.
That is why, today, I have introduced legislation and a resolution to get to the bottom of what Elon Musk and DOGE are doing with our data and how they are using artificial intelligence.

ICYMI: I introduced an Oversight Resolution to investigate Elon Musk and DOGE’s unsanctioned data mining of our private and secure data and the use of artificial intelligence. 
 
The American people deserve to know why Elon Musk and DOGE are hacking our data and what they’re doing with it. We will get to the bottom of this!

And yesterday, I heard Marjorie Taylor Greene, I was standing on the Floor while she gave a speech on this very language that is in this bill that would literally say that states and localities cannot enforce their own data rules or AI. It preempts federalism. It preempts state law. It would prevent states from protecting their own citizens.

So, you mentioned that part of why this deregulation language is in here that would preempt state and local laws regarding the regulation of AI systems is, in part, be- cause of this $500 million request that is in the bill. Can you help us understand what would that $500 million be used to do specifi- cally? [...] Ms. S TANSBURY. Just some specifics, like, what kind of systems would be built with this $500 million?

Anthropic’s Claude 4 model attempted to blackmail the people it believed were trying to shut it down, and then it would ignore and other ones would ignore shutdown commands, even when told in advance that shut down commands were coming, and went as far as to rewrite itself and preserve itself on a different server to avoid the com- mands of the humans in charge of it.

Friends, this week was wild. From the Trump and Musk breakup to reconciliation which would not only gut healthcare and food assistance but strip the courts of enforcement tools and allow tech companies to circumvent AI and data laws across the country, to the egregious DOGE rescission package that guts billions in foreign assistance, the WHO, UN, and PBS and NPR—there’s a lot to talk about.

But, we must also celebrate the good this week. There’s a lot at stake—but we're in the fight together. Stay strong. And, keep showing up for our communities!

Yesterday, the Supreme Court’s majority ruled that DOGE could access our social security data. But, we don’t know what DOGE and the Administration are actually doing with our data. What we do know is they’re working with private AI companies to integrate data in ways we’ve never seen before with far-reaching implications.

That’s why we’re fighting back against AI language in the reconciliation bill that would strip states and local governments from protecting us. On this one—even @RepMTG and I agree.

We must stop this language from passing before it’s too late.
that basically would preempt state and local laws from regulating our private data through AI systems.

Are we in a sci-fi movie? Is this the Twilight Zone?

Unfortunately, it’s worse. Because this is real life, and what is happening here is dangerous.

Not only is our data at risk due to DOGE and the Administration—but Congress itself is currently trying to deregulate AI and data privacy protections across the country in the big abomination of a bill.

Remember when Elon Musk and his DOGE associates hacked and downloaded our data to train his private AI system?

The NYT found that he still has a stake in 449 companies that deal with AI. His decisions in the White House directly affect those companies and his bank account. 

That’s why earlier this year, @SenWarren and I introduced the SGE Ethics Enforcement & Reform (SEER) Act of 2025, which would expand and strengthen ethics and conflict of interest rules for all Special Government Employees. 

Enough is enough with this corrupt Administration.
